clue.text: Goddesses of a thousand customs

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
customs are habits or usages, so uses

explanation.surface: A scholar describes the many rituals observed by a pantheon of goddesses.
explanation.definitionFit: The nine Greek deities who inspire the arts, such as Calliope and Clio, are the classic goddesses of crossword clues.

clue.text: Fears condensation corrodes

parts.note: mist is fine condensation of water droplets
metal that corrodes rusts

explanation.surface: Someone worries that damp is eating away at their metalwork.
explanation.definitionFit: To fear someone will betray you is to doubt or distrust them, a synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Big bloomer, having wild fun in more leisurely setting

indicators.note: in tells us the scrambled letters sit within the word for more leisurely

parts.note: more leisurely means slower

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of fun run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener's tall flower enjoys some wild fun in a relaxed backyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns FUN into UNF, which goes 'in' SLOWER after its S; 'setting' just rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall plant with huge yellow heads is a big bloomer, a playful way to say a large flowering plant.

clue.text: Southern wood of window frame

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A carpenter picks a southern timber to build a window frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The sliding glazed frame of a traditional British window is called by this name.

clue.text: One who always pockets litter?

parts.note: read as a tidy person stuffing rubbish in their pockets, but the litter is a brood of young carried in a pouch

explanation.surface: A conscientious walker stuffs every scrap of rubbish into their pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo or wallaby carries its young, its litter, in a pouch, which defines this mammal group.

clue.text: Cup-tie monitor troublesome in film

indicators.note: troublesome suggests the letters are unruly and get rearranged

explanation.surface: A football referee's monitor causes trouble during a cup tie, much like a dramatic film.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema film is also known as a moving picture, the longer phrase for a movie.

clue.text: Employer in trousers

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie inside the word trousers

explanation.surface: A boss is found wearing trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who employs or makes use of something is one who uses it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: One mile past is as far as a moth can get

definitions.text: as far as a moth can get

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
past, as in years past, means ago

explanation.surface: A moth flutters a mile beyond its limit and can go no further.
explanation.definitionFit: The final, fully adult winged stage of an insect's development is the furthest a moth gets in its life cycle.

clue.text: Hen, perhaps, always carried in both hands?

indicators.note: carried in says one piece is held within another, as in two hands

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, both hands
aye is an old word for always, as in for aye

explanation.surface: A hen is carried carefully in both hands, as it always is.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen that produces eggs is an egg-producer, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Inner charnber of society in America

parts.note: taken as written
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A secret inner room belongs to an exclusive American club.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity in the skull behind the nose is an air-filled chamber inside the head.

clue.text: Tommy's home in Ireland a long way off, going by air

definitions.text: Tommy's home in Ireland a long way off, going by air

parts.words: Tommy's home in Ireland a long way off, going by air
parts.note: Tommy is a British soldier of the First World War, whose marching song says it is a long way to this Irish town; going by air hints at the tune, an air

explanation.surface: A homesick soldier's Irish town is far away and must be reached by plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The song 'It's a Long Way to ...' was sung by British troops, nicknamed Tommies, in 1914; 'air' is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: This County in Ireland is the town of the famous wartime marching song sung by British soldiers.

clue.text: Particular English clergyman of Salisbury, at one time

parts.note: particular, meaning fussy and proper, gives prim
a minister is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A fussy English cleric serves in the cathedral city of Salisbury.
explanation.walkthrough: Salisbury looks like the cathedral city, but here it is Lord Salisbury, who led three Victorian governments.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Salisbury was head of the British government three times, so he was once its leader.

clue.text: Bank on river, next to cathedral

parts.note: Ely is an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A riverbank sits beside a great cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests a riverbank to go with 'river', but 'Bank on' is a verb meaning trust.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on something is to depend on it, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Theme of leading Olympic finalists

parts.note: leading, as in first place, means top

indicators.note: finalists points to the final letters of the word Olympic, the last two

explanation.surface: The subject for discussion is the top Olympic finalists.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a subject under discussion, a synonym.

clue.text: Get up with the lark?

parts.note: reads as rising early, but means climbing into the sky like a lark in flight

explanation.surface: An early riser gets up at dawn when the birds start singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Larks rise high in song flight, so to rise into the sky like one is to fly upwards.

clue.text: Mild Black Country

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a country is a land

explanation.surface: The Black Country, an industrial area of the English Midlands, is called mild.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Country is an industrial part of the West Midlands; here the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Mild food or manner is unexciting and gentle, a synonym.

clue.text: Jaunty through Kentucky

parts.note: per means through or by means of
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: Someone travels cheerfully through the state of Kentucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaunty means lively and cheerful, a synonym.

clue.text: Pool cared for, kept in good condition

parts.note: a well is a pool or source of water
something cared for and kept safe is preserved

explanation.surface: A village pond has been looked after and is in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept in good condition looks young or undamaged for its age, the same idea.

clue.text: Clever tin-working in this part of ticker

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Clever work with tin produces a part for a mechanical clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ticker' looks like a watch, but it is slang for the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is slang for the heart, and one of its four chambers is a part of it.

clue.text: Girls for whom the guards turn out?

indicators.note: turn out suggests the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Soldiers parade in honour of some girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' looks like guards parading, but it scrambles THE GUARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Female offspring are girls in relation to their parents.

clue.text: Naive young person, easily scared after leap?

indicators.note: after places the word for easily scared behind the word for leap

parts.note: a leap is a spring
chicken means cowardly, easily scared

explanation.surface: A timid youngster panics after jumping.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inexperienced and naive is often called young and green, the idiom used for youth.

clue.text: Dot finds a cat

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Dot, a woman's name, discovers a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot' reads as a woman's name but means a tiny particle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a tiny speck, and the smallest unit of matter is a tiny particle.

clue.text: Could be a nutmeg is mostly used in savoury jelly

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: nutmeg is an example of a spice, as 'Could be' signals

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether nutmeg is mainly used in a savoury jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' marks nutmeg as an example of SPICE; 'mostly' drops its last letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to glaze cold dishes.

clue.text: Norma possibly work overtime?

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
split as over + time: over sets the next piece below in a down clue, and an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Norma might be working overtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Norma looks like a woman's name, but it is Bellini's opera; 'overtime' splits into over + time.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellini's Norma is an example of a staged musical drama, as 'possibly' signals.

clue.text: Amoretto in court, surrounded by policemen

indicators.note: surrounded by tells us the court phrase sits within the police letters

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, detectives
up, as in up before the judge, means in court

explanation.surface: An Italian liqueur is in court, surrounded by police.
explanation.walkthrough: Amoretto suggests the almond liqueur, but it is a little cherub, a love god.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a small winged cherub in art, the figure of the god of love.

clue.text: Opening for Henry to join Circle Line

parts.note: an arc is a curved line, a part of a circle
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry joins the Circle Line on the London Underground at an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here it means a curved line.
explanation.definitionFit: An archway is an opening in a wall, a synonym.

clue.text: Type of morbid appetite

definitions.meaning: a size of printing type, twelve points
a craving to eat non-food substances such as earth or chalk

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a size of print and an abnormal craving for non-food items.

clue.text: Pungent smell rising, one gives a little bite

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tang is a sharp, pungent smell or taste

explanation.surface: A sharp smell rises from something that bites.
explanation.definitionFit: A small biting fly gives a small bite, a playful description.

clue.text: Ford once here carried fish

indicators.note: carried means the word for here holds the fish inside it

parts.note: present means here, in attendance
id or ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An old Ford vehicle once carried a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Ford suggests a car, but it is Gerald Ford, the American leader of 1974-77.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Ford was the head of the United States in the 1970s.

clue.text: The Hole in the Wall in scenic Herefordshire

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie inside the words scenic Herefordshire

explanation.surface: A pub called The Hole in the Wall stands in a pretty part of rural England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hole in the Wall is a common pub name; here it is a recess.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess in a wall for a statue or ornament is a hole in the wall, literally.

clue.text: Kidney card

definitions.meaning: kidney means nature or type, as in men of that kidney
a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person's nature or sort and an odd, colourful person.

clue.text: Rows and drops on face, one hears

indicators.note: one hears means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: tears are drops on the face when crying

explanation.surface: A sad scene of quarrels and tears, as someone overhears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' could mean quarrels, which suits the tears, but it means ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows of seats in a stadium are ranks set one above another.
